lifecycle: Clock: t = server time now - the occurrence's publishedAt (an event) or the phase's startedAt (a stage). Never a local start time, never an animation's end. The server's endsAt and expiresAt are unchanged by any presentation.

Late load or reconnect: if t >= the film's end, draw the final state at once (no replay); if 0 <= t < end, seek to t; a stage presentation (capsule, vote result) snaps to its current pose. Never replay a historical death, Sync or cinematic.

Duplicates: key every presentation by its event id (or phase id); one id plays once per page. A repeated or older viewRevision draws nothing new. An event past expiresAt (publishedAt + 30 s) never starts.

Cancellation: a newer viewRevision that changes what a presentation shows (a seat moved, a phase ended) cancels it: remove its nodes and draw the latest authoritative state. Cancelling never changes game state.

Precedence: terminal result > Sync > Captain commands > medical outcome (death before rescue at one berth) > attack, Blackout and blocked > movement and placement > ambient idles. A higher presentation starting in the same region cancels a lower one to its final state; different regions (another room panel) play concurrently.
Hidden tab: pause nothing on the server; on return compute t again from the server clock and seek or snap. Audio never plays in a hidden tab.

Interaction: press areas, name tags, room labels, timers, Pass and navigation never move, scale or hide for a film; a film may darken or shake only the art layer. Pointer events pass through every film layer.

Reduced motion: honoured at load and when changed during playback (a change mid-film switches to the reduced variant at the same t). Reduced variants carry the same information with fades of 80-120 ms, no travel, camera, shake, flash, particles or spin.
Audio: public events only, from the cue sheet (never only inside a video); muted by the device setting; private, room-filtered and pair-private presentations play no public audio by default.
Asset failure: a missing picture or video never blocks: the scene's static final state (or its words in the live region) stands alone.

requests.ask: A presentation window for BLACKHOLE_SYNCED: the event is published at the Sync checkpoint and the next phase (JAIL_VOTE, 60 s) starts at once. Either a fixed post-Sync stage (e.g. 5 s, like VOTE_RESULT) or confirmation that the display may overlay the vote's first 5.2 s while phones show only the 2.4 s band over the board (never over the ballot controls). Until answered, the pilot assumes the overlay and the server's vote endsAt is unchanged.

The exit: the conversation's end is HACK's endsAt and the next phase starts at once. Confirm the display may show the 2.8 s exit page over the next phase's first seconds, or keep S2's board-only exit on the display too.

RESCUED carries seatIds, location, slotId and clinicalAnchor: enough. Confirm the published snapshot's placement of a rescued patient (still at the berth, or back in a room, as the 1.8.0 fixtures had it), so the film ends on the right figure; the pilot handles both.

MOVEMENT_COMPLETED and PLACEMENT_CHANGED carry seatIds, location and slotId but not the origin slot: a walk needs the previous finalized placement (the client keeps the last snapshot). Confirm that a reconnecting client without the previous snapshot snaps instead of walking.

Neutral shared transit: navigation.lastMovedRound and arrivedAt are public; a neutral "the ship moved" presentation needs nothing else. The office-private route view (privateNavigation) needs the previous position to animate a step; confirm it may be derived from the previous view.

Promise result transitions (Pending to Fulfilled / Not fulfilled / Condition not met) need the evaluation moment: confirm promises[].status changes arrive with a viewRevision at the evaluation (voting start after Sync).
A shown drawing's arrival: windows[].drawings[] has order and round but no publishedAt; a stamp-in needs the moment it was shown, or the client stamps on first sight only (no replay on reconnect).

P14 gives the Engineer a private confirmation of the fixed identities, but the player view has only abilities.engineerSpent. Add the Engineer's own record, e.g. abilities.engineerCapture { round, seatIds } (Engineer only), so the confirmation shows the identities the server fixed at registration, never the client's preview (someone may move between the two). Until then the file says only that the capture was used.

abilities.shipHackSpent cannot tell a hack registered this round (still to apply at this round's navigation) from one used in an earlier round. Add abilities.shipHackRound (Hacker only) so the file can say "applies at this round's navigation" or "used in Round N". Until then a spent hack is drawn as used, its round unnamed.
